<!-- conventions:begin claude.intro -->
Claude Code conventions for this repository. The rules live in `.claude/rules/`
(`workflow.md`, `architecture.md`, `coding.md`, `knowledge.md` always apply;
`pitfalls.md` collects recurring traps; a `commands.md` per app holds its CI
sequence). Hooks, skills and agents come from the `conventions` plugin, not
from this repo. `AGENTS.md` (OpenAI Codex) is generated from these rules: edit
them, never `AGENTS.md`; `knowledge.md` and `pitfalls.md` serve both tools.
<!-- conventions:end claude.intro -->

## Stack

| App | Path       | Stack                                                                | Verify                          |
| --- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| web | `apps/web` | TanStack Start, oRPC, TanStack Query, Tailwind + shadcn (`@repo/ui`) | `.claude/rules/web/commands.md` |

<!-- conventions:begin claude.branches -->
## Branches

`main` is **production** (reached from `staging` through `demo` by merge-commit promotion PRs, ADR 0006; release-please runs there). `staging` is
the integration branch. **Every PR targets `staging`, never
`main`.** A PR against `main` is wrong whatever
it contains — retarget it before reviewing.

    git switch staging && git pull && git switch -c feat/my-change
    /conventions:pr
<!-- conventions:end claude.branches -->

<!-- conventions:begin claude.commands -->
## Commands

- Verification = the app's `commands.md` sequence, run through
  `/conventions:verify-app <app|all>` before claiming a task done.
- Dependencies: `pnpm add -E <pkg>` (exact pin, latest
  stable from the registry); never hand-edit a manifest or lockfile.
- `/conventions:pr` opens the PR (size cap 400 lines / 15
  files, stacked PRs beyond); `/conventions:test-gaps` lists untested changes;
  `/conventions:adr` records a long-term decision; `/conventions:release` prepares
  `staging → main`; `/conventions:deps-audit` fixes advisories.
<!-- conventions:end claude.commands -->

## .claude/rules/architecture.md

# Architecture

<!-- conventions:begin architecture.structure -->
- **Feature-first.** A feature owns its slice — `domain/` → `application/` →
  `infrastructure/` → transport/UI — under one directory. Code two features
  need lives in `shared/`, never in either of them.
- **One registration point.** A feature plugs in through one factory listed at
  the composition root (the on/off switch); nothing self-registers on import.
- **Injected, never global**: logger, clock, id generator, database, config.
  Config is parsed once at boot into a typed object; a missing or invalid
  variable stops the process before it serves. Nothing else reads the env.
- **A new layer, folder convention or cross-feature dependency** the rules do
  not cover → ADR first (`/conventions:adr`), code second.
<!-- conventions:end architecture.structure -->

- **One accepted global**: `globalThis.$rpcServerClient`, the in-process oRPC client for
  server-side rendering (oRPC's "Optimize SSR" pattern, ADR 0011). Only the composition root
  sets it; only `shared/client/rpc-client.ts` reads it. No other global.

<!-- conventions:begin architecture.ports -->
- **Ports and adapters everywhere.** Never reach an external dependency (DB,
  HTTP API, filesystem, clock, mail, vendor SDK) directly — go through a port
  owned by the application layer and named after the business need, not the
  technology; the adapter lives in infrastructure with an in-memory twin for
  tests. Swapping a service = a new adapter, nothing else.
- **Layers never call each other directly.** Direction is domain ← application
  ← infrastructure ← transport/UI; wiring only happens in the composition
  root named in the app's rules (`.claude/rules/<app>/`). No concrete import
  crosses a ring: a lint error there means move the code, never silence it;
  where no linter enforces the direction, the rule still applies.
- **Business decisions are pure domain functions** — a test of them needing a
  mock means logic leaked into an adapter. Use case: refuse → validate → act.
  Entities are immutable: a state change returns a new value, and creation
  goes through a factory that checks the invariants.
- **A use case has one entry point** and receives its ports as injected
  dependencies. It never calls another use case (extract a domain service)
  and never receives a request, a session or an ORM type.
- **Plain data crosses the boundaries.** Use cases take and return DTOs;
  entities never leave the application layer. Two mappings, one place each:
  contract ↔ DTO in the transport handler (validate → authorize → use case →
  map), domain ↔ persistence in the adapter's mapper.
<!-- conventions:end architecture.ports -->

<!-- conventions:begin architecture.boundaries -->
- **No cross-feature import**: a feature imports `shared/` and its own ports,
  never another feature; client code imports server code as types only
  (`import type`). Only infrastructure names a vendor (ORM, SDK, driver);
  only the composition root or the feature's factory picks the adapter.
- **Another app or service is consumed through its API** behind one fetch
  layer — that layer is the adapter; pages and handlers never call its SDK
  or import its source.
- **Concurrency invariants live in the database** (unique constraints,
  conditional updates); isolation + retry is the second line; a parallel test
  is the proof an in-memory twin cannot give. Effects that leave the
  transaction (notify, wake a worker) run after commit, never shape the result.
<!-- conventions:end architecture.boundaries -->

<!-- conventions:begin architecture.testing -->
- **Every change is tested.** Domain + application: written test-first, unit
  tests with in-memory twins, never mocks of internals. Adapters: integration
  tests against real infrastructure (a test that skips silently when its env
  var is unset does not count — set it, run it).
  Transport: route/contract tests. A PR touching source with no test says why.
- The **Test layout** table below is project-owned (`--refresh` never rewrites
  it): one row per layer, paths relative to the app dir. `/conventions:test-gaps`,
  `test-writer` and `rules-reviewer` read it to place a file's test; the
  optional `other` row is the fallback for files matching no other glob.
<!-- conventions:end architecture.testing -->

## Test layout

Mirrored layout: a test sits at the source path under `tests/unit/`, minus the `server/` and
`client/<kind>/` segments of a feature (`src/features/<f>/server/domain/x.ts` →
`tests/unit/features/<f>/domain/x.test.ts`). Paths are relative to the app dir.

| layer | source glob | test dir | test kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| domain | `src/features/*/server/domain/**` | `tests/unit/features/*/domain` | unit |
| application | `src/features/*/server/application/**` | `tests/unit/features/*/application` | unit (in-memory twins) |
| infrastructure | `src/features/*/server/infrastructure/**` | `tests/unit/features/*/infrastructure` | contract (`tests/contracts/<port>.contract.ts`) |
| rpc | `src/features/*/server/rpc/**` | `tests/unit/features/*/rpc` | unit (procedures called without HTTP) |
| client | `src/features/*/client/**` | `tests/unit/features/*/client` | dom (jsdom project) |
| shared | `src/shared/**` | `tests/unit/shared` | unit |
| e2e | `src/routes/**` | `tests/e2e` | end-to-end (Playwright, production build) |
| other | `src/**` | `tests/unit` | unit |

## App layout (every `apps/*`, ADR 0010)

- A feature is exactly `server/{domain,application/ports,infrastructure,rpc}`,
  `client/{api,hooks,components,pages,copy.ts}`, `schemas.ts`, `index.ts` (client entry),
  `server.ts` (server entry, `create<Feature>UseCases` factory) and `testing.ts` (test twins).
  Anything else fails `ARCH-LAYOUT` (`apps/web/tests/architecture/layout.test.ts`).
- Cross-feature code lives in `src/shared/{domain,server,client}`.
  `src/shared/server/composition-root.ts` is the only file that binds ports to adapters and the
  only file that reads `process.env` (through `loadEnv` in `shared/server/config/env.ts`).
- Adding a feature = copying the demo feature folder, its tests, and one line each in
  `shared/server/rpc/router.ts` and `composition-root.ts`. Removing it = the reverse.
- Import rules are lint errors with a stable id (`biome.jsonc`, `scripts/biome/*.grit`); each
  rule has a violating and a compliant fixture in `apps/web/tests/architecture/rules.test.ts`:
  - `ARCH-LAYER` — a layer imports only itself and inner layers (domain ← application ←
    infrastructure ← rpc); page routes never import `shared/server`; `routes/api/` imports only
    `shared/server/composition-root` from it.
  - `ARCH-FEATURE` — no feature imports another; `shared/` imports a feature's `server.ts`
    only from the composition root and the RPC router; routes import a feature's `index.ts`.
  - `ARCH-CLIENT-SERVER` — client code imports server code with a top-level `import type`
    only (inline `import { type X }` is rejected); Start import protection is the build backstop.
  - `ARCH-VENDOR` — vendor SDKs only in `server/infrastructure/` and `shared/server/adapters/`;
    the list is the regex in `scripts/biome/vendor-sdks.grit`.
  - `ARCH-REEXPORT` — `export … from` only in a feature's `index.ts`, `server.ts`, `testing.ts`.
  - `ARCH-RELATIVE` — no `../` import inside an app; use `@/…`.
- A new layer, feature entry or rule updates `biome.jsonc`, the fixtures, the layout test and
  ADR 0010 in the same PR. A lint error from these rules means move the code, never suppress it.

## .claude/rules/clean-architecture.md

# Clean architecture (every `apps/*`, ADR 0003)

How the generic rules of `architecture.md` map onto a feature's `server/` folders.

- **Domain** (`server/domain/`): entities and value objects with a `create` factory that checks
  the invariants and throws a business error; immutable (a change returns a new value); no
  import of a framework, `zod`, `@orpc/*` or any vendor package (`ARCH-VENDOR`). Business errors
  of the feature live in one `<feature>-error.ts` and extend the `shared/domain/errors.ts`
  taxonomy.
- **Application** (`server/application/`): one class per use case, one `execute` method, ports
  injected through the constructor. Ports are interfaces in `application/ports/`, named after
  the business need (`GreetingRepository`), never after a technology. Cross-feature ports
  (`Clock`, `IdGenerator`) live in `shared/server/ports/`. A use case returns a DTO built by a
  mapper in the application layer; an entity never leaves it.
- **Infrastructure** (`server/infrastructure/`): adapters implementing the ports. Every port has
  an `in-memory-<port>.ts` twin; every adapter of a port runs the same contract suite
  (`tests/contracts/<port>.contract.ts`), so the twin and the real adapter cannot drift.
- **Transport** (`server/rpc/<feature>-procedures.ts`): a `create<Feature>Procedures(useCases)`
  factory; each procedure validates its input with the feature's `schemas.ts`, calls one use
  case and returns its DTO. No business decision in a procedure, no error mapping per feature
  (the shared base procedure maps errors, see `errors.md`).
- **Wiring**: `server.ts` exports `create<Feature>UseCases(deps)`, the only file outside
  infrastructure that names an adapter. `shared/server/composition-root.ts` calls it once per
  process with the shared adapters and the validated settings; the router mounts its procedures.
- **Settings**: a feature declares its environment variables in `server.ts`; the composition
  root validates every declared variable at startup and refuses to start, naming each invalid
  one. Code under `features/` never reads `process.env`.
- **Tests**: domain and application are tested with in-memory twins and fixed clocks or id
  generators from `testing.ts`; never a mock of an internal module.

## .claude/rules/coding.md

# Coding

<!-- conventions:begin coding.changes -->
- **Search before creating** (`ast-grep`, LSP, grep): reuse > extend > add new.
  Duplicating behaviour that already exists is a defect, not a style issue.
- **Stay in scope** (no drive-by refactor, rename or reformat — its own PR);
  library and API questions are answered from current docs, never memory.
- **Fit the existing architecture.** When the clean solution needs the
  structure reshaped, stop and surface the trade-off — never bolt on an
  exception. Adding a feature = copying the closest existing slice, layer by
  layer, plus its registration entry — never a fresh layout.
- **No scaffolding**: no placeholder, `TODO`, speculative branch, "just in
  case" flag, or unused export, type or parameter. Where `commands.md` names a
  dead-code checker it is the judge; elsewhere grep for a consumer first.
- **A schema change ships with its migration in the same PR** — never a
  permanent read-time fallback. The migration is idempotent and resumable
  (proven by a test), touches only its owner's tables, never edited after merge.
  Its SQL is read before applying: no unintended `DROP`, column removal, type
  narrowing or `NOT NULL` without a backfill.
- **Build clean before "done"**: zero errors and zero warnings across build,
  type-check, lint and tests — a warning left behind is a defect.
<!-- conventions:end coding.changes -->

<!-- conventions:begin coding.style -->
- **Brace every `if`/`else`**, even single-line. The loop exit condition is
  visible in the header — no `while (true)` with an inner `break`.
- **Path aliases over relative climbs**: `@/…`, never `../../`. Code,
  comments and identifiers are English.
- **Expected failures are one typed business error** (a kind that maps to a
  status, a code the caller branches on); anything else is logged with an
  incident reference and shown generically. Error classes live in `errors.ts`,
  never in the file that throws them. A `catch` never drops the cause.
- **No unexplained type escape** (`any`, a cast hiding a mismatch, `!`, an
  ignore comment). Comments say why, never restate the code.
- **Log through the injected logger**, never `console.*`; a secret or an
  auth header never reaches a log line.
- **User-facing text lives in a message catalogue**, never as a literal in a
  handler or component; the default-language entry is mandatory.
- **UI is mobile-first** (tap targets ≥ 44px, no hover-only affordance); a
  mockup is implemented pixel-perfect — ask on ambiguity, never improvise.
- **Factories are `create*`**; a feature's public entry is one file
  (`module.ts` / `index.ts`), the only file outside infrastructure that may
  name an adapter.
<!-- conventions:end coding.style -->

<!-- conventions:begin coding.dependencies -->
- **A vendor SDK appears only under infrastructure**; domain, application and
  UI depend on ports (adding one: `workflow.md`, exact pin through the
  package manager, never a hand-edited manifest).
- **Workspace packages are built before any app typecheck or build** — apps
  do not rebuild them on install. A change to a shared package or contract is
  a cross-app change: verify every consumer, not only the one you touched.
- **Generated files are never hand-edited** (ORM clients, import maps,
  vendored UI primitives): regenerate with their tool, keep them out of lint,
  and when they are not committed the verify sequence generates them first.
  Compose around a vendored component, never edit the file.
- **A major version bump of a toolchain piece** (language, bundler, framework)
  is its own PR; a ceiling recorded in `pitfalls.md` is not raised without
  re-running the case that set it.
<!-- conventions:end coding.dependencies -->

## .claude/rules/errors.md

# Errors and logging (every app and package)

- **No silent error.** A caught error is handled (the code continues with a stated fallback) or
  rethrown. A `catch` that only logs logs at `warn` or above with the original error attached and
  a comment saying why the flow continues. Empty `catch` blocks and `.catch(() => {})` are
  defects.
- **One business-error taxonomy.** Expected failures extend `DomainError`
  (`src/shared/domain/errors.ts`): a `kind` the transport maps and a stable SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE
  `code` the client maps to copy. The error's `message` is English, for logs only, never shown.
- **One mapping point.** `mapErrors` in `src/shared/server/rpc/errors.ts` turns a business error
  the caller can fix into `BAD_REQUEST` with `data: { code }`, and any other error into
  `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` with `data: { referenceId }`, logged once with that reference. A
  procedure never builds an `ORPCError` itself and never leaks a stack or an internal message.
- **Shared schemas speak in codes.** A zod issue message in `schemas.ts` is a business code, so a
  rejected input reaches the client in the same `{ code }` shape as a domain error.
- **Explicit to the user.** The client maps every known code to a sentence in the feature's
  `client/copy.ts` (a `satisfies Record<Code, string>` keeps the map complete) that names what
  failed and what to do. The generic message is only for unexpected errors, and shows the
  reference id when the server returned one.
- **Structured logs only**, through the injected `Logger` (`shared/server/logging/logger.ts`):
  one JSON object per line, context in fields, never `console.*`, never string concatenation.
  Errors are logged once, at the boundary that handles them; inner layers throw.
- **Never in a log or an error message**: secrets, tokens, cookies, authorization headers,
  personal data beyond an id. The logger redacts secret-looking field names; do not rely on it
  for values placed in the message text.

## .claude/rules/knowledge.md

# Capturing knowledge while working

<!-- conventions:begin knowledge.adr -->
- **Long-term choice made during a task** (new dependency category, storage
  format, ownership boundary, protocol between apps, anything a future dev
  would ask "why?" about) → run `/conventions:adr` before opening the PR.
  ADRs live in `docs/adr/NNNN-<slug>.md`; the most recent one is the model.
- **An accepted ADR is a rule** with the weight of `.claude/rules/`; a
  proposed one is guidance; an ADR's open points are not rules yet. A change
  that contradicts an accepted ADR follows it or adds a superseding ADR in the
  same PR, which also sets the old one's status to superseded.
<!-- conventions:end knowledge.adr -->

<!-- conventions:begin knowledge.pitfalls -->
- **Same error hit twice, or a trap that cost more than a few minutes and is
  not obvious from the code** → append an entry to `.claude/rules/pitfalls.md`
  in the same PR: `- YYYY-MM-DD — <symptom> → <cause> → <fix>` (≤ 3 lines).
- Keep `pitfalls.md` under 40 lines: when an entry is stable and app-specific,
  move it into that app's rule file and delete it from pitfalls.
- Do not record: linter/type errors, one-off typos, things the tests already
  explain.
<!-- conventions:end knowledge.pitfalls -->

<!-- conventions:begin knowledge.rules -->
- **Where a new rule goes**: generic (holds for any app) → the matching file
  here; app-specific → `.claude/rules/<app>/` (written by
  `/conventions:app-rules`), one line per fact with its evidence path. A rule
  already stated in the generic files is never repeated in an app file.
- **A rule states a constraint, a boundary, a prerequisite or a trap** — never
  what a reader sees in the code. A guide longer than three lines goes under
  `docs/` and the rule links to it.
<!-- conventions:end knowledge.rules -->

## .claude/rules/pitfalls.md

<!-- conventions:begin pitfalls.header -->
# Pitfalls — recurring traps (append, date, keep short)

Format: `- YYYY-MM-DD — symptom → cause → fix`. See `knowledge.md` for when to add.
<!-- conventions:end pitfalls.header -->
- 2026-10-29 — SSR loader fails with "fetch failed" behind a port-forward, container or proxy → the
  server called `/api/rpc` over HTTP at the browser's Host → SSR uses the in-process client the
  composition root registers (`globalThis.$rpcServerClient`, ADR 0011); never self-fetch.
- 2026-10-29 — `demo → main` promotion conflicts (for example on `.release-please-manifest.json`)
  → the release commit reached `staging` only squashed, so `main` was never an ancestor of `demo`
  → the release workflow also back-merges `main → demo` with a merge commit (ADR 0006); if it did
  not run, merge `main` into `demo` through a `chore: merge main into demo` PR.

## .claude/rules/ui.md

# UI (every app, ADR 0007)

1. **shadcn first, minimal hand-written HTML.** Every control is a `@repo/ui` component
   (`import { Button } from '@repo/ui/components/button'`). Order: an existing `@repo/ui`
   component; a composition of them in the feature's `client/components/`; a new shadcn component
   added to `packages/ui`; a custom component only when no shadcn item covers the need, with a
   header comment saying why. Hand-rolled buttons, inputs, alerts and card-like `div`s are
   defects. `packages/ui` components are owned code (ADR 0007), not vendored: change them there, once,
   never per screen.
2. **Sizes and variants are props.** `size` / `variant` only; no height or padding overrides on
   `@repo/ui` components. Tap targets are the package's job: the default `Button`, icon `Button`
   and `Input` are 44 px (`h-11` / `size-11`); never use a smaller size for a primary touch
   control. `w-full` only where the layout needs it (for example a submit button on phones,
   `w-full sm:w-auto`).
3. **Tokens only.** Semantic Tailwind tokens from `@repo/ui/theme.css` (`bg-primary`,
   `text-muted-foreground`, `text-destructive`, `border-border`…). Never hex values, palette
   colours (`gray-*`, `zinc-*`) or arbitrary `[#…]` colours.
4. **View / ViewModel split.** A View (`client/components/`) renders props and calls callbacks:
   no data fetching, no state beyond local presentation. A ViewModel (`client/hooks/use-*.ts`)
   owns state, queries, mutations and actions, and returns exactly the View's props. A page
   (`client/pages/`) composes ViewModels and Views; a route file only mounts the page and runs
   its loader.
5. **Forms: zod + `useReducer`, no form library.** The feature's `schemas.ts` holds the zod
   schema shared with the procedure input; the ViewModel validates with it before submitting,
   keeps the form state in a `useReducer` with an explicit status (`idle`, `invalid`,
   `submitting`, `succeeded`, `failed`) and ignores results of superseded submissions.
6. **Data**: reads go through the route loader (`ensureQueryData`) and the same query options in
   the ViewModel, built from the oRPC TanStack Query utils in `client/api/`; a mutation
   invalidates the queries it changes. No `fetch` in a component.
7. **Copy lives in `client/copy.ts`**, English only, never as a literal in a component; error
   copy is keyed by business code (`errors.md`).
8. **Accessibility**: every input has a `Label`; a field error is linked with `aria-describedby`
   and announced (`role="alert"`); a request-level error uses `Alert`; one `h1` per page.
9. **Mobile-first, then desktop.** Layout starts at phone width and adds `sm:` / `md:` variants;
   no hover-only affordance, no horizontal scroll at 375 px.
10. **Before "done"**: the screen is checked at 375 px and at desktop width, every interactive
    element is at least 44 px on touch, and the end-to-end test of the flow passes.

## .claude/rules/workflow.md

# Workflow

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.branches -->
## Branches

- `main` = production (reached from `staging` through `demo` by merge-commit promotion PRs, ADR 0006; release-please runs there). `staging` =
  integration branch. **Every PR targets `staging`.** Release =
  deliberate PR `staging → main` via `/conventions:release`.
- Branch off the integration branch:
  `git switch staging && git pull && git switch -c feat/<name>`.
  Branch names are `<type>/<kebab-case-slug>`, `<type>` from the commit types.
- Never commit directly on `main` or `staging`;
  never force-push (the plugin hooks refuse both).
<!-- conventions:end workflow.branches -->

- Release flow (ADR 0006): feature PRs are squash-merged into `staging`; promotions
  `staging → demo → main` are merge-commit PRs, never squashed or rebased; release-please opens
  the release PR on `main`, then back-merge PRs `main → staging` (squash) and `main → demo`
  (merge commit) merge themselves.
- Commit and PR titles are checked by commitlint (`pr-title` job); scopes are optional.
- Required checks on `staging`, `demo` and `main` = the CI job names `check`, `pr-title`, `e2e`,
  `agents-md` (`.github/rulesets/*.json`). A renamed or added job changes all three rulesets in
  the same PR, and the maintainer re-runs `scripts/setup-repo.sh` after the merge to apply them.
- The `agents-md` job checks out `Azurioh/claude-conventions` at the commit in
  `CONVENTIONS_SHA` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). Dependabot does not track it: bump it by hand
  to the plugin commit in use (`git -C ~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/claude-conventions
  rev-parse HEAD`), regenerate `AGENTS.md` and commit both together.

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.commits -->
## Commits

- Format `<type>(scope): description` — types: feat, fix, refactor, docs,
  test, chore, perf, ci, release. English only.
- One logical change per commit. No `wip` / `fix typo` / `address review`
  commits in a PR — fold them first: `git commit --fixup` +
  `git rebase --autosquash`.
- **Never commit without the user's OK.**
- Never push or open a PR without the user's OK for that change, and never
  merge into `staging` or `main`: the human merges.
<!-- conventions:end workflow.commits -->

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.pr -->
## PR hygiene

- Open every PR with `/conventions:pr`, never a raw `gh pr create`. Title uses
  the same `<type>(scope): description` format. Body states what/why, the
  verification command that was run and `Closes #N` when an issue is linked.
  Titles, bodies and review comments are English.
- **Size cap: ≤ 400 changed lines (additions + deletions) and
  ≤ 15 files**, excluding lockfiles, generated migrations and
  vendored UI components (`prSize.exclude` in `.claude/conventions.json`). The
  `pr-size` hook blocks `gh pr create` beyond the cap unless
  `--label large-pr` is passed explicitly (mass renames / generated
  code only).
- Bigger change → **GitHub native stack** via `/conventions:pr --stack`: one
  branch + PR per logical group, branch names describe the content (never
  numbered), linked with `gh stack link --base staging <branches
  bottom→top>`. GitHub shows the order, diffs per layer and retargets bases
  automatically on merge.
<!-- conventions:end workflow.pr -->

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.deps -->
## Dependencies

- New dependencies are added exact-pinned at the latest stable version from the
  registry: `pnpm add -E <pkg>` (the `deps-exact` hook
  refuses the unpinned form). Existing caret ranges are not retrofitted. Never
  hand-edit a manifest or a lockfile.
- Security advisories on transitives → `/conventions:deps-audit` (direct
  dependency bump first, override/resolution pin for transitives).
<!-- conventions:end workflow.deps -->

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.worktrees -->
## Shared worktrees

- Never bare `git stash` / `git stash pop` (the stash stack is shared across
  worktrees). Use `git stash push -u -m <tag>`, then
  `git stash list --format='%H %gs'` to find it, then `git stash apply <sha>`.
<!-- conventions:end workflow.worktrees -->

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.verification -->
## Verification and discovery

- CI parity per app: the sequence in `.claude/rules/<app>/commands.md`
  (single-app repo: `.claude/rules/commands.md`), run in file order from the
  repo root. `/conventions:verify-app <app|all>` runs it — do this before
  claiming a task done.
- Cross-cutting rules: structure, boundaries and tests in `architecture.md`;
  change discipline, style and dependencies in `coding.md`; test gaps →
  `/conventions:test-gaps <app|all>`.
- Long-term choices → `/conventions:adr`; recurring traps → `pitfalls.md`
  (see `knowledge.md`).
<!-- conventions:end workflow.verification -->

- Layer mapping and wiring → `clean-architecture.md`; error taxonomy and logging →
  `errors.md`; UI components, forms and tap targets → `ui.md`.

<!-- conventions:begin workflow.agents-md -->
## AGENTS.md (Codex)

- `AGENTS.md` is generated from `CLAUDE.md` + `.claude/rules/**` (the plugin's
  `agents-md` hook reruns the generator on every rule edit). Never edit it by
  hand: change the rule, and the next generation carries it to Codex.
- `knowledge.md` and `pitfalls.md` are shared by Claude and Codex — a trap
  recorded by either one is read by both.
<!-- conventions:end workflow.agents-md -->

## Scoped rules

Before touching a file matching a glob, read the rule file of its row.

| when you touch | read |
|---|---|
| `apps/web/**` | `.claude/rules/web/commands.md` |
